segments.segment_summary: A close-up shot pans across a cardboard stencil with the words 'FOOD CYCLIST' cut out. The stencil has been spray-painted with bands of blue and green paint and is resting on a wheel.

key_moments.caption: A close-up view of the word 'FOOD' on the stencil, showing the spray paint texture.
The camera pans right to reveal the full 'FOODCYCLIST' text.
The camera tilts up, creating a bright lens flare from the sun.

segments.segment_summary: A man stands outside in a sunny, grassy area and explains the importance of using multiple light coats of spray paint when stenciling to avoid drips and preserve the stencil.

key_moments.caption: A man with a beard and fleece vest begins speaking to the camera, with a bright sun flare behind him.
He gestures with his hand while explaining how to apply paint to the stencil.
A close-up of the man's face as he talks about spray painting the other side of the stencil.

segments.segment_summary: The video shows both sides of the spray-painted cardboard stencil as the man explains that painting both sides prevents the cardboard from curling as it dries, thus preserving the stencil for longer use.

key_moments.caption: A shot shows the back of the stencil, lightly sprayed with red paint, with the text mirrored.
The stencil is flipped over to show the front side again, revealing the full 'FOODCYCLIST.COM' text.
The man explains that the drying paint pulls on the cardboard, causing it to curl.

segments.primary_activity: giving tips and promoting a website
segments.segment_summary: The man provides further tips for stenciling, recommending using a staple gun to hold the cardboard in place for a cleaner result. He then concludes the video by promoting his website while standing in front of his chicken tractors.

key_moments.caption: He mimes using a T50 hand stapler to secure the stencil to a surface.
He warns that holding the stencil by hand while spray painting can lead to a crooked result.
A graphic for 'FarmMarketingSolutions.com' appears on screen as he begins his outro.
The man smiles at the camera as he finishes speaking, with chicken tractors visible in the background.
